property.description: Value-add retail investment at 3904-3914 Augusta Rd, Greenville SC. Four tenants currently in place at ~$9.99/SF.

legal_basis.point_of_sale_trigger: Conveyance by deed constitutes assessable transfer of interest (SC Code §12-37-3150(A)(1))
legal_basis.reassessment_cap: 15% per 5 years does NOT apply to assessable transfers (SC Code §12-37-3140(B))

current.estimated_millage_note: ESTIMATED — Greenville County combined millage (county ops + school + other). Needs county confirmation. Range: 0.320-0.380.

post_sale.verdict: MODERATE — tax roughly doubles (2.3x, not 50x as NJ model incorrectly predicted)
post_sale.impact_on_noi: Claimed NOI $66,000 − tax increase $9,758 = adjusted NOI ~$56,242

comparison_to_nj_model.nj_model_error: NJ model used 2.5% on 100% of FMV. SC uses 6% assessment ratio × millage rate. The NJ model overstated post-sale tax by $3,300 (19%).

leases.occupancy_note: Listed as Vacant but mentions 4 tenants — contradiction

hard_asset_floor.methodology: Land: 1.40 acres @ $5-8/SF retail corridor = $305-490K. Building: 7,500 SF Class C insured @ $30-45/SF = $225-338K. Combined low/mid/high.

Worst Case \u2014 Tax Bomb + Tenant Exod.description: Post-sale taxes double to ~$17.3K. 2 tenants leave. NOI drops to $30K. Exit cap 9%. MOIC 0.58x at $575K invested.

Baseline \u2014 Tax-Adjusted Status Quo.description: All 4 tenants stay at $9.99/SF. SC reassesses at sale → NOI $56.2K (down from $66K claimed). Exit cap 8% after 5yr. Value $625K.

Phase 1 Optimize \u2014 Rent Bumps + Tax.description: Push rents from $9.99 to $13/SF market. Appeal tax assessment down to ~$500K (60% of FMV). NOI recovers to $62.5K. Exit cap 7.5%.
Phase 1 Optimize \u2014 Rent Bumps + Tax.probability_note: 25% — achievable with active management in growing corridor

Phase 2 Expand \u2014 Renovate to Class.description: $50K renovation. Full occupancy at $14/SF Class B. Exit cap 7%. Capital invested $625K.

Phase 3 Strategic \u2014 Parcel Assembly.description: 1.40 acres on Augusta Rd. Assemble adjacent parcels. Moonshot redevelopment value. Not counted in best-case convexity.

Phase 1 Optimize \u2014 Rent Bumps to Ma.description: Push rents to $13/SF. Tax settles at ~$15K/yr. NOI $72K. Exit cap 7.5% on improved property. Value $900K.

market.metro_growth: Greenville is among fastest-growing Southeast metros
market.corridor_context: Augusta Rd described as blooming retail corridor near I-85

dimensions.name: Traffic & Visibility
dimensions.rationale: 229' frontage on Augusta Rd. Dedicated turn lane. Freeway visibility from I-85 (100/100 traffic score). Pylon sign. 30,000+ VPD on Augusta Rd.

dimensions.name: Corridor Growth Trajectory
dimensions.rationale: Augusta Road described as 'blooming retail corridor.' Greenville is one of the fastest-growing metros in the Southeast. Near I-85 — the primary commercial artery between Atlanta and Charlotte.

dimensions.name: Parking Ratio
dimensions.rationale: 30 spaces / 7,500 SF = 4.0 spaces per 1,000 SF. Retail standard is 3-4/1,000. Above standard — rare for Class C.

dimensions.name: Rent-to-Market Gap
dimensions.rationale: In-place rents at $9.99/SF vs market $13-14/SF. 30-40% mark-to-market upside. Greenville retail rent growth 3-5% annually.

dimensions.name: Land Banking Value
dimensions.rationale: 1.40 acres on Augusta Rd with I-85 proximity. Land value in this corridor is appreciating. 0.12 FAR means significant redevelopment optionality (could build up to ~7,300 SF more).

dimensions.name: Tenant Stickiness
dimensions.rationale: Equilibrium Zen Gym (fitness — sticky, hard to relocate) + Gaston Security Group (B2B services — stable). Both are destination-based, not impulse. But only 2 confirmed tenants of 4.

dimensions.name: Price-to-Replacement
dimensions.rationale: At $110/SF ask ($73/SF at $550K target), well below replacement cost of $120-150/SF for comparable retail construction in Greenville. Replacement would cost $900K-$1.125M.

dimensions.name: Zoning Optionality
dimensions.rationale: C2 zoning allows broad commercial uses — retail, office, service, restaurant. But no residential or mixed-use by-right. Would need variance for higher-value use.

retail_moats.verdict_text: STRONG MOAT — 22/24. The property sits on a high-visibility, high-growth corridor with rare parking abundance and a 30-40% rent upside. The moat is location-driven: Augusta Rd frontage with I-85 access is not replicable. Main vulnerability is tenant concentration risk with only 2 confirmed occupants.
retail_moats.moat_narrative: This is a LOCATION moat, not a tenant moat. The value isn't in the current rent roll ($9.99/SF below-market tenants) — it's in the 1.40 acres on Augusta Road with 229' of frontage, freeway visibility, and ample parking. The play is: buy below replacement cost, push rents to market, and let the corridor's growth compound the land value. The tenants are placeholders, not the thesis.
